nrIncident.summary: Disruption in the Barking area until at least the end of Tuesday 10 November: amended Suffragette line service, and no trains between Barking and Grays via Rainham (Essex)
nrIncident.routes:
c2c between London Fenchurch Street and Grays / Laindon / Pitsea / Leigh-on-Sea / Southend Central / Thorpe Bay / Shoeburyness, between London Liverpool Street and Shoeburyness, and also between Barking and Grays / Southend Central
London Overground between Gospel Oak and Barking Riverside
nrIncident.message:
On Friday 23 October, a freight train partially derailed between Woodgrange Park and Barking. Some lines remain closed as significant damage has been caused to the railway infrastructure.
As a result, some trains through Barking will be cancelled or revised. Where trains do operate, they may be subject delays of up to 10 minutes.
• London Overground are running a reduced service on the Suffragette line between Gospel Oak and South Tottenham, and no trains will run between South Tottenham and Barking Riverside
• There will be no c2c service between Barking and Grays via Dagenham Dock, Rainham (Essex), and Purfleet
Disruption is expected until at least the end of the day on Tuesday 10 November.
A visual disruption map video is available.
c2c customer advice:
No services are calling at Dagenham Dock, Rainham or Purfleet.
Trains which normally call at Stratford (London) and London Liverpool Street will divert, and call at West Ham and London Fenchurch Street instead. These trains typically operate after 20:30 each evening, and at weekends.
Your ticket will be accepted at no extra cost on:
• Elizabeth line services between London Liverpool Street and Romford
• First Essex buses between Grays and Stanford-le-Hope
• Greater Anglia between London Liverpool Street and Southend Victoria
• London Buses between Barking, Dagenham Dock, Rainham, Purfleet and Grays
• London Buses Superloop SL12
• London Underground District line between Barking and Upminster, Jubilee line between West Ham and Stratford (London), and Liberty line services between Upminster and Romford
Replacement buses are running from 05:00 between Upminster and Grays, calling at Rainham, Purfleet and Grays.
Replacement buses are running from 05:25 between Grays and Upminster, calling at Purfleet, Rainham and Upminster.
Passengers for Dagenham Dock can travel on the EL2 bus service at no extra cost.
London Overground customer advice:
Service is suspended between South Tottenham and Barking Riverside.
A reduced service will run between Gospel Oak and South Tottenham as follows:
• Services will depart Gospel Oak at xx:09 and xx:39
• Services will depart South Tottenham at xx:13 and xx:43
Your ticket can be used at no extra cost on:
• London Buses via any reasonable route
• London Underground via any reasonable route
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.
You can find the pick-up and drop-off location of rail replacement services by checking station signage or by searching for your station on our Find a Station page.
Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

nrIncident.message:
A fault with the signalling system between Watford Junction / Willesden Junction and Clapham Junction means that lines are blocked.
Trains operating between these stations will be cancelled or revised.
This is expected until 07:30.
London Overground customer advice:
Some services will be diverted to Richmond.
Your ticket can be used on London Buses via any reasonable route, at no extra cost, in order to complete your journey.
Southern customer advice:
Trains are unable to run between Watford Junction and Shepherds Bush. This is due to a signal failure in the Mitre Junction area. If you require stations between Watford Junction and Shepherds Bush, you will need to use an alternative route.
Services between Clapham Junction and Shepherds Bush will likely be busier than normal, as only Southern services are currently running on this route.
The following stations will not be served by Southern services at this time:
• Wembley Central
• Harrow & Wealdstone
• Watford Junction
Make sure you leave at least an additional 30 minutes to complete your journey.
Service alterations:
The following service changes are expected:
• Trains that usually run between East Croydon and Watford Junction will run between East Croydon and Shepherds Bush. If you require stations between Shepherds Bush and Watford Junction you will need to use London buses. You can use your existing ticket on these services at no extra cost
Please ensure to check before you travel using our online journey planners and live departure boards for the latest information.
Planning your journey:
For help planning your journey, check live departure boards, view a live network map or see alternative route guides.
If you’re travelling within London, you can use the TfL Journey Planner.
Can you tell me more about the incident?
A fault with a signal system is affecting trains on the route between Watford Junction and Shepherds Bush.
Signals tell train drivers when it’s safe to continue into the next section of track. The signalling system will show a green light when the track is clear for a long distance ahead, and drivers will then be shown one or two yellow lights to warn them when they are approaching a red signal. This means that they can anticipate the amount of braking that's required to stop before they reach another train or any form of problem on the line.
If a signal develops a fault, it may be unable to show the normal sequence of coloured lights. The signalling system is designed to keep trains safe when this happens, so the affected signal will show a more restrictive indication. Drivers may need to stop and get permission from the signaller before continuing, or travel at a reduced speed through the affected area.
These additional safety measures mean journeys through the area take longer and can cause trains to queue behind one another. In severe cases, services may need to be cancelled, revised or diverted to prevent delays from building up across the wider network.
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and will work to repair the affected equipment. Once the fault has been fixed and the signalling system is working normally, trains will be able to run as usual and the scheduled service can begin to recover.
